lines.en: As both the school day and my counseling hours come to an end, I’m left with nothing to do but mindlessly roam the halls in hopes of encountering someone or something.

And while it is true that I carry a small, electronic device that enables me to create opportunities for things to happen, I find that it’s often more interesting to let the world decide my schedule instead.
As such, here I am — alone and melancholic, letting the warm sun creep through the windows and illuminate my body with the light and luster of longing and loss.
What I long for is a way to fill this void with something that won’t sink through my stomach when I lie in bed tonight.
What I’ve lost is the will to make that happen.
: Ngh!
Or have I?
: Ngh......mmngh!

I enter the library and come face to face with what I’m pretty sure is my first soirée into the cliché, yet realistic trope of a short girl trying to reach something on a shelf that’s just a little too high.
This, of course, opens up a window of infinite choices on how I’m going to tackle the situation.
Would it be best to just stand here and wait for her to ask for my help?
Should I take the more aggressive and dramatic approach of lifting her up and letting her grab her desired book on her own?
Or should I maybe plunge this world into total chaos, knocking the shelf completely over and potentially killing Uta in the process?
The possibilities are endless.
: Nnnghhhhh!!
But if I don’t do something soon, Uta could dislocate or permanently damage her arm- which would make it harder for her to provide daily handjobs to me when we are ultimately married.
So, I guess I’ll cut her some slack and lend a hand so that I may one day fully experience hers.
: Huh? Where’d you come from?
: Which one are you trying to reach?
: Oh. Uhh...that red history book a little to the right. I can’t really see the full title from all the way down here.
: And you were reaching for it anyway? Since when is your interest in history that pure?
: My interest in history doesn’t exist. I just texted Futaba asking which one covers some of the stuff Imani’s been teaching us lately and...this is me following her directions.
: Or trying to at least. She forgot to mention this book had a height requirement.
: Here. This one, right?
: Yeah. That’s the one.
: What do you want in return, though?
: Return?
: I know how this works, Sensei. You hand me the book. Then I try to thank you. Then you say something like, “Thanks ain’t enough, sugar. There’s somethin’ else I’m after, ” while staring at my body.
: You could have at least made the dialogue more...me-like. I can’t really envision ever calling anyone “sugar.”
: Just tell me what kinda prize you’re after so I can figure out whether or not the book is of equal value.
: I was going to give it to you out of the kindness of my heart. But now, I’m curious as to what I can actually get for it.
: You were gonna do something out of the kindness of your heart? Even though this is the exact type of tropey situation guys like you dream about? I’m surprised you didn’t just pick me up.
: You should be happy I didn’t pick you up. If I did, who even knows when I’d be willing to put you down again?
: So you’re after the whole package after all, huh?
: Or just a kiss.
: Huh?!
: Why does that embarrass you more than the “whole package?”
: That package doesn’t include kissing!
: What does it include then?
: A night of fiery passion, a morning of deep regret, several moments of intense pelvic pain, and a phone call to my parents! Nobody ever said anything about kissing!
: In that case, I will take one night of fiery passion. Thanks.
: No, that doesn’t work either! I was just listing the contents! I never agreed to the fiery passion!
: Just take the book, Uta.
: Can I?
: Yeah. Like I said, I planned on doing this out of the kindness of my heart and was fully prepared to keep all of my fantasies about you to myself.
: Just...out of curiosity...are we talkin’ like...one or two fantasies? Or...
: You’re missing about ten zeros.
: Ten...zeros?
: I said what I said.
: That’s...
: That’s a lot of fantasizing...
: I’m starting to think you don’t even want this book.
: Do you really...
: A-hah!
: “A-hah” what? Why am I being “A-hah”ed?
: You’re just messing with me! You think throwing out a huge number with ten zeros will get me to compromise and give you some kind of consolation prize! I know your tricks!
: There are no tricks. You’re just a little delusional and very sexually repressed.
: That may be true! But the library isn’t the place to discuss it!
: Shall we take this outside then?
: Outside?! Are you an exhibitionist?!
: I can be.
: I knew it!
: So, do you get like this every time someone gets something off of a shelf for you?
: We all do. Everyone knows that us short girls wait our entire lives for tall people like you to walk by and remind us of all the things we can’t do on our own. It really gets us going.
: Wow. I really should have just picked you up, huh?
: I...I can’t think of a safe way to answer that question, so I’m just going to take my book now! Thank you!
Uta snatches the book out of my hands and retreats to the corner of the library to...presumably read it.
But seeing as the world has decided that she will be the one to fill my void today, I have other things in mind.
: You’re...staying with me?
: Is that a problem?
: It’s not a problem. I just thought it was kind of obvious that I need to study, so...I don’t want to bore you or anything.
: I’ll never be bored while I’m looking at you, Uta.
: Could you maybe...stop saying stuff like that to me? Just...Just for today, I mean. I’m not going to be able to focus if you’re all...flirty like that.
: Why do you need to focus in the first place? Do you actually, like...care about learning all of a sudden?
: I don’t really have much of a choice. I’ve been getting a lot of extra work from Imani lately so I can catch up to everybody else and stay in the class.
: Stay in the class? Did she threaten to kick you out or something? Because I’m pretty sure that’s above her pay grade.
: I think it’s more of a testing...formality thingy than her actually wanting to get rid of me. Our grades for all those important school-wide tests get sent to our parents and mine...well...
: Let’s just say they aren’t really the happiest when it comes to my performance. Which...is fair. I’ve been slacking off.
: Do you...need my help?
: Hm? No. I appreciate the offer, but I’ll manage on my own. I get too distracted in groups.
: Well, that’s a relief because I know next to nothing about history and wouldn’t have been much help anyway.
: You already did your part by being tall. Uta-chan can handle the rest. But if you want to sit there and watch her while she reads, she’ll let you do it for cheap.
: How about I just help instruct Uta-chan in the subjects that I do specialize in instead?
: Is this the part where you make a biology joke?
: No.
: It was, wasn’t it?
: You don’t know me.
: No, but I do know your tricks. And I’m not about to let you get the upper hand on me again when I’ve practically lived on the...lower...hand?
: Why is “upper hand” a thing but not “lower hand?” Who comes up with phrases like that?
: Again, this isn’t really an area of expertise for me. But feel free to inquire if you have any questions about cute girls or obscure poets.
: Quite the specializations you’ve got there. Figured there’d be a few more given your age and experience though.
: There are. You just get a little too flustered whenever I talk about them.
: Hahah...hah......hah.....you must be...confusing me with someone else.
: Right, yeah. I’m probably thinking about the other Uta. If you’re Uta-chan, you’re probably not interested in me at all, right?
: Did...did somebody tell you that...normal Uta is?
: Nope. Just a hunch.
: I figure if normal Uta is interested in me, though- it’s only a matter of time until she cracks since her best friend has already given her the blessing to go ahead and make some moves.
: And I...think you might be...misreading the situation a little, but...
: But that’s a...topic for another day! Hahah! Look at us, pretending to be all...whatever...whatever that was just now.
: You used “flirty” a few minutes ago. I feel like that sums it up well enough.
: Yeah, but...you’re like that with everybody. Is it really flirting if that’s just your default setting?
: I feel like you would know, if anyone. You’re the one who’s figured out a way to monetize that setting. And, on top of that, you have another one you can switch to after work. I envy that.
: You shouldn’t. It’s a lot more exhausting than I make it look. And most of the time, I’m kind of just...internally screaming.
: About what?
: (Screaming internally)
: (Screaming internally and also horny)
: Oh...nothing in particular...
: B-Besides! I’m sure there are plenty of other people who you’d like more than me. And I’m not just talking about Io or any of your other girlfriends this time either.
: Did Io get promoted to “girlfriend” status without my knowledge?
: That’s hard to say...
: I know you two haven’t, like...kissed and stuff yet. But I also know she actually, like...talked to you.
: About...her thing....
: She certainly did. Right around the same time the possibility of a triad was brought up.
: Probably goes without saying, but...Io doesn’t...talk about that kind of stuff with just anybody, Sensei. You must be really special to her if she felt comfortable enough to admit all that.
: You did the same thing, didn’t you? Admitted something about your past that you have trouble looking back on.
: But my thing was me being young and stupid. Io was never at fault for anything she did.
: Neither were you.
: Huh?
: Like you said, you were young and stupid. Expecting you to make rational decisions back then would be a little...unreasonable.
: You got caught up in a feeling and did something you felt like you should do. That’s more of an accident than something done with true intent.
: But it’s still...it’s still something I did. That I pay the price for.
: I get that. But I’d look at you the same way whether or not any of that happened.
: Let’s...you know...we, um...
: Another topic...this one is...I’m starting to feel a little...uh...
: Uhh...Dorm Wars! How did you...
: How did you feel about this year?
: It was...different. It felt more like our regular beach trip but with a few contests sprinkled in. I might just be saying that this time since there were several that didn’t involve me, though.
: I agree. I think it worked for Halloween since that’s normally just a one day event, but there were a lot of girls on the beach who kind of just wanted to relax for the weekend.
: Some of the contests went pretty well, though. Like...the swimsuit one was pretty fun. And Io told me she enjoyed herself with the raft thingy. Plus, Futaba’s horror story was actually pretty cool.
: Now...Nodoka’s on the other hand...
: I don’t know if I was just...maybe expecting a little too much since she’s apparently an amazing writer or...or if I just didn’t get it, but...
: I can’t really wrap my head around whatever hers was supposed to be.
: Do you have any thoughts, Sensei? You seemed pretty interested once she finished, so I figured that maybe there was a part of it you got that I was just too dumb for.
: Sensei?
: It’s weird.
: It definitely had some sort of effect on me, but I can barely remember any of it and...it’s hard to put into words what the effect even was.
: Maybe it was one of those open-ended thingies? Somethin’ that people are supposed to interpret in...different ways? Like...like psychic readings or something. Do you believe in that stuff, Sensei?
: Not even remotely.

: Is that so? That’s a shame. Uta-chan was about to offer you a special palm-reading and it could have been the only chance you’ll ever get to touch her. Too bad you don’t believe in her psychic powers.
: Do you believe in psychic powers, Uta?
: Mmm...I guess a little. No more or less than most girls my age, I think.
: I’m sure a lot of it is fake, but I think there’s gotta be some kind of truth to it. Even if it’s just kinda...manifesting whatever it is the psychic tells you further down the line.
: The problem with believing things in a roundabout way like that is that you’ll never really be able to prove yourself right or wrong. You’ll always just be stuck with a “maybe.”
: Why is that a problem?
: It’s less of a problem and more of just...a depressing uncertainty. Like, what do you gain from living your life under the pressure of so many “what ifs?”
: Well...for me, it’s like...what if the truth is...the opposite of what you want?
: What if the thing you find out winds up making it even harder to be the person you were before you found out?
: So what if people believe in a thing that isn’t actually there? If believing in that thing makes them happy, I say go for it. You don’t need a definitive answer- just a little hope and...
: And the knowledge to know when you should probably stop listening.
I stop listening.
Uta’s affection has increased to [uta_love]!
